figures.name: breadth_ranks
figures.caption: The breadth above the species. Left: eukaryote taxa at each rank, NCBI's named ones (a species: a binomial, no placeholder or hybrid; a higher taxon: one holding such a species), those NCBI holds a genome of, and Eukore's (with a genome; with any record). Right: per group, Eukore's taxa with a genome of NCBI's with one (a higher taxon counts in every group one of its species is of).

figures.name: content
figures.caption: The markers one species links. Left: the species holding each marker kind from any source (their genome, a RefSeq organelle genome, a published read) and from their genome's own assembly; ITS: ITS1, 5.8S and ITS2 on one record; operon: 18S to 28S on one record. Right: per group, the species holding it from their own assembly, of all the group's species.

figures.name: upset
figures.caption: The species by the databases that hold them: each bar the species exactly those databases hold (the dots below; the largest combinations, and what Eukore holds alone), blue where Eukore is one of them; left, each database's species. A database's species are those NCBI names (its names matched to NCBI's); ROD and BUSCO's dataset, Eukore's own sources, are left out.

figures.name: novel
figures.caption: The species a genome is the first sequence of a marker for. Left: per marker, the species Eukore holds it of from their genome's own assembly, and those of them that none of the marker's references the build read names (by name, synonym or taxid: an upper bound, a reference may name a species otherwise). Right: their share per group.

figures.name: agreement
figures.caption: Where Eukore and another database hold the same species' marker: the records that agree with Eukore's genomes' sequence, those that are another species' gene (one of the two is misnamed) and those unlike the species' own genome's (agreement_records.tsv lists both). EUKARYOME's and ROD's reads by the build's own-species check, MIDORI2's by its reference screen, PR2's and SILVA's 18S and UNITE's ITS by alignment to the genomes' own 18S and ITS (97% or more alike to the species' own genome's agree).

figures.name: quality
figures.caption: The records each check flags, per group: the genomes (NCBI's and its FCS-GX and ANI reports' flags, copies another clade's, a duplicated genome, a genetic code that differs), the BUSCO copies, the rRNA records and the organelle genes (the checks that flag the most, then the confidence tiers low, medium and unverified); each cell the share of the group's.

figures.name: thresholds
figures.caption: The identity that parts taxa, per marker and rank: the cutoff with the best balanced accuracy between the sequences that should stay together (a species: the intraspecific panel's least alike pair of its own assemblies; a higher rank: the copies whose nearest other species shares it) and those that should be apart (the copies whose nearest other species does not). All BUSCOs together, the 18S, each BUSCO (small dots).

figures.name: tree
figures.caption: The tree of the BUSCO proteins against NCBI's taxonomy (tree.py: up to two species' genomes per genus, the loci Single in the most of them placed on BUSCO's profiles, FastTree). Left: NCBI's taxa with two genomes or more that are one branch of the unrooted tree. Right: the tree, the groups of its tips along it (bands), the genomes placed apart from their taxon marked.

figures.name: growth
figures.caption: The release's genomes by the year NCBI released their assemblies (bars), and those released by then (line); dashed, the other databases' release dates where benchmarks/databases.tsv gives them: what a database frozen then could not hold.
